mechanism_narrative: A higher federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with negative 5-day S&P 500 returns due to increased discount rates on equity cash flows, as evidenced by the negative correlation between FEDFUNDS and 5-day returns over historical data.
failure_condition: The correlation between FEDFUNDS and 5-day returns is not negative (correlation >=0) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in CPIAUCSL above 3.5% signals persistent inflation, prompting market concerns about future monetary tightening and leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The average 20-day return when CPIAUCSL YoY change > 3.5% is not significantly negative (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 0.2 percentage points and fall in industrial production (INDPRO) below 0.5% signals an economic slowdown, leading to negative 60-day S&P 500 returns as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The average 60-day return when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp and INDPRO falls > 0.5% is not significantly negative (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), the S&P 500 experiences negative 20-day returns due to heightened risk aversion and reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: The average 20-day return during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0% is not significantly negative (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts (HOUST) level above 1500 thousand units signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: The average 20-day return when HOUST > 1500.0 is not significantly positive (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 (2017=100) signals a contraction in manufacturing output, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to concerns about corporate earnings and economic growth.
failure_condition: The average 20-day return when INDPRO < 100.0 is not significantly negative (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS) above 720000 million dollars and housing starts (HOUST) above 1500 thousand units signals robust consumer demand, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as the economy expands.
failure_condition: The average 20-day return when RSAFS > 720000 and HOUST > 1500.0 is not significantly positive (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% signals the Federal Reserve will implement monetary easing, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as lower interest rates boost equity valuations.
failure_condition: The average 20-day return when UNRATE > 4.5% is not significantly positive (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.
